cases.name: proofs_from_other_session
cases.mutation: use the proof files of another session of the same point

cases.name: reps_swapped
cases.mutation: pass rep1's proof as rep0 and the reverse

cases.name: rep1_second_round_coin_low_bit
cases.mutation: flip bit 0 of coin 5 of round 1 of <t>/rep1

cases.name: rep0_mid_round_coin_low_bit
cases.mutation: flip bit 0 of coin 0 of round 70 of <t>/rep0

cases.name: link_point_changed
cases.mutation: flip bit 0 of coordinate 0 of link point 0

cases.name: publics_digest_changed
cases.mutation: set link.publics_sha256.<t> to 32 zero bytes

cases.name: round_message_digest_changed
cases.mutation: set streams[0].rounds[0].msg_sha256 to 32 zero bytes

cases.name: require_link_false
cases.mutation: set config.require_link to false

cases.name: other_instance_file
cases.mutation: verify against another point's public input

cases.name: unused_high_bits_of_query_coin
cases.mutation: flip bit 127 (the top bit of hi) of coin 0 of the last round of <t>/rep1
cases.why: query indices use only the low bits of each coin (§13); a verifier that rejects this reads bits it must not

cases.name: zerocheck_coin_low_bit
cases.mutation: flip bit 0 of coin 0 of round 0 of <t>/rep0
cases.why: see §19: which coins an honest proof's checks do not depend on

cases.name: last_coin_low_bit
cases.mutation: flip bit 0 of coin 0 of the last round of <t>/rep1

cases.name: rep_root_differs
cases.mutation: set root_sha256 of <t>/rep1 to another value

cases.name: third_rep_stream
cases.mutation: duplicate <t>/rep1 as <t>/rep2

cases.name: lone_rep
cases.mutation: delete <t>/rep1 and its proof entry

cases.name: extra_round
cases.mutation: append a copy of the last round to <t>/rep0

cases.name: child_stream
cases.mutation: add a stream <t>/rep0/f0 with zero rounds

cases.name: root_f_not_sigma
cases.mutation: set link.root_f to 32 zero bytes and root_f_sha256 and link_sha256 accordingly

cases.name: proof_byte_flip
cases.mutation: flip one byte of the rep0 proof and set its proof_sha256 accordingly

cases.name: fast_params_relabel
cases.mutation: rewrite commitment.params.profile in the rep0 proof to Fast and fix proof_sha256

file_negatives.note: The first 12 cases ran on two cells with the recorded outcomes; the remaining 8 are new record-level cases this spec adds (their outcome under upstream is recorded in phase 2; upstream_expect marks the two intended divergences D1, D2 of PROTOCOL.md §17.1). The six rec_residuals_* cases (§16.10, D13) refuse a rec-residuals/… unit that is not the verifier's part net, the five rec_sparse_* cases a rec-sparse/… unit that is not the verifier's sparse-phase net, and the six rec_opening_* cases a rec-opening/… unit that is not the verifier's opening part net; upstream takes the unit as the file gives it.

forgeries.dump_plan: Add `--dump DIR` to the selftest subcommand of flock-pure-gpu, flock-ir-frame and the PR #83 circuit-statement binary so every case writes its session.json and proofs; run once on a CPU pod at 8 VUs (a few minutes); preserve the tree as one artifact; each case's expected verdict is its selftest `pass` line.

replayable.note: Replayable (record, proofs) sets for the circuit statement, one per statement version (Flock.Tags), generated with the vectors patch of that PR #83 commit; both verifiers run on the same directories (README.md, agree.py). A set with `lean_refuses_drawn` has sessions drawn by a law no soundness claim draws by (D12): the Lean verifier refuses each session whose record carries a unit draw with that reason at setup (one that does not set up, for that first), and upstream must give it its expected verdict (`agree.py --lean-refuses-drawn`). A set with `lean_refuses` is a statement form the soundness proof does not cover (PROTOCOL.md §16.15, D12), and one with `lean_refuses_drawless` has sessions without a draw (D12): the Lean verifier refuses each session they cover (every session not refused at setup, and each without a draw) with that reason once every check has passed, the form's first. Such a session passed every check and is compared as accepted, any other verdict as it is (`agree.py --lean-refuses`, `--lean-refuses-drawless`).
